s1.syndrome_frame: Severe respiratory infection with subsequent ocular involvement
salient_findings: Blurred vision and redness in one eye
Relative afferent pupil defect and central scotoma
Peripapillary hemorrhages and retinal vessel narrowing
key_facts: Hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia in March 2020
Recent close contact with a fatal case
No relevant medical history reported
Developed blurred vision and redness in one eye on day 2 post-admission
Temporary pain when mobilizing the globe
Best-corrected visual acuity was +2 logMAR (hand movement) OD and 0 logMAR OS
Normal complete blood cell counts
Normal serum angiotensin-converting enzyme levels
Negative results for syphilis, HIV, Toxoplasma gondii, and Borrelia serologies
Positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2
Negative CSF SARS-CoV-2 RT-PCR
Cranial MRI with fine optic nerve cuts showed normal results

shortlist.label: COVID-19
shortlist.why_kept: Patient was hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia and had a positive nasopharyngeal swab RT-PCR for SARS-CoV-2, suggesting a link between the respiratory infection and subsequent ocular involvement

shortlist.label: Optic neuritis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient developed blurred vision, redness, and pain in one eye, with findings of relative afferent pupil defect, central scotoma, and impaired color and contrast vision, consistent with optic neuritis

shortlist.label: Retinal vasculitis
shortlist.why_kept: Fluorescein Angiography showed fluorescein leakage from retinal venules, indicating retinal vasculitis, which can be associated with various infectious and inflammatory conditions

shortlist.label: Varicella-zoster virus retinitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had a weakly positive IgG for VZV, and VZV retinitis can cause ocular symptoms similar to those experienced by the patient

shortlist.label: Cytomegalovirus retinitis
shortlist.why_kept: Patient had a weakly positive IgG for CMV, and CMV retinitis can cause ocular symptoms similar to those experienced by the patient, particularly in immunocompromised individuals

raw.rationale: The patient was hospitalized for severe bilateral pneumonia in March 2020, had recent close contact with a fatal case, and tested positive for SARS-CoV-2, which suggests a strong link to COVID-19. The development of blurred vision and redness in one eye, along with other ocular symptoms, could be related to COVID-19-associated ocular manifestations.

rejected.label: Optic neuritis
rejected.why: While the patient has some symptoms consistent with optic neuritis, such as blurred vision and pupillary edema, the presence of other ocular findings like retinal vasculitis and the context of COVID-19 infection make it less likely as the primary diagnosis.

rejected.label: Retinal vasculitis
rejected.why: The patient does have fluorescein leakage from retinal venules, indicating retinal vasculitis, but this could be a secondary manifestation related to the primary diagnosis of COVID-19.

rejected.label: Varicella-zoster virus retinitis
rejected.why: The patient had very weakly positive IgG for VZV, but the clinical presentation and the context of recent COVID-19 infection make this less likely as the primary cause of the ocular symptoms.

rejected.label: Cytomegalovirus retinitis
rejected.why: The patient had very weakly positive IgG for CMV, but there's no strong evidence to suggest CMV retinitis, especially given the negative results for HIV and the clinical context of COVID-19.
